# Migration 0001 — Shared Identity and Academic Context Implementation Specification

**Document ID:** PULSE-DB-M0001-SPEC-001  
**Version:** 1.0.0  
**Status:** Owner-approved Option B design direction — revised executable migration preparation authorized; remote application not authorized  
**Date:** 2026-11-07  
**Logical migration:** M0001  
**Filename:** To be generated by supabase migration new after approval

## 1. Objective

Establish the canonical PULSE identity and academic-context foundation that System A references. System A must not create a second institute/tenant, user/person, student, centre, batch, membership or role authority.

M0001 is the first logical migration in the unified PULSE migration plan. It is not a commitment to retain the existing numeric filename 0001_identity_and_academic_context.sql; the executable timestamp must be generated by the Supabase CLI after the canonical branch and migration sequence are selected.

## 2. Scope boundary

### In scope for the shared foundation

- Tenant identity.
- Canonical person identity.
- Mapping from Supabase Auth subject to canonical person.
- Tenant-person association.
- Student identity anchored to a canonical person and tenant association.
- Centre and batch identity.
- Effective-dated academic context/enrolment history.
- Tenant-safe composite keys and foreign-key strategy.
- Minimum internal constraints and indexes needed to preserve identity integrity.

### Explicitly out of scope

- System A assignment/source catalogue/workflow tables.
- System A student obligations, report events, observations, verification, correction and doubt.
- QBMS question content or question authoring.
- DTE taxonomy, classification or difficulty records.
- Parent/guardian access policy and field-level read projections until OPEN-009 and OPEN-025 are closed.
- Full role-to-permission bundles and application RLS policies until authorization decisions are approved.
- Teaching assignments unless OPEN-018 is resolved and owner explicitly includes them in M0001; default sequencing places them in M0003.
- Data backfill from legacy systems; this spec assumes a verified empty application schema unless a separate backfill plan is approved.

## 3. Canonical entity contract

| Entity | Responsibility | Required semantic rule |
|---|---|---|
| tenants | Institute/organization boundary | One tenant identity; not duplicated in System A |
| people | Human actor identity | Stable person ID independent of Auth UID and tenant membership |
| person_auth_identities | Auth subject mapping | Auth UID is an authentication identifier, never the business actor key |
| tenant_memberships | Person's association with a tenant | Association is not a role or permission grant; it is independent of student identity |
| tenant_role_grants | Authorization capability grant | Separate, effective-dated, revocable, scope-aware authority; physical design subject to OPEN-015 and OPEN-019–021 |
| students | Tenant-owned student domain identity | Mandatory tenant_id; nullable person_id referencing people.id when a person link is known; no membership requirement |
| centres | Tenant-owned academic location | Centre identity belongs to tenant; no System A duplicate |
| batches | Tenant-owned cohort | Batch belongs to tenant and optionally to a centre |
| academic_context_epochs | Effective-dated student academic context | Historical epochs retained; valid interval and batch relationship tenant-safe |
| teaching_assignments | Teacher-to-resource scope | Resource assignment is distinct from role capability; defer to M0003 unless explicitly approved for M0001 |

The exact columns, keys and cardinalities must follow the approved physical blueprint after OPEN-014 through OPEN-018 are closed. This table is an entity contract, not a complete DDL definition.

## 4. Required invariants

1. A person may have multiple Auth identity mappings only if provider/subject uniqueness and lifecycle rules explicitly permit them; one Auth subject must never resolve ambiguously to multiple people.
2. Auth subject mapping is server-trusted. User-editable Auth metadata must not determine tenant, person, student or role authorization.
3. tenant_memberships expresses person-to-tenant association only; it is independent of student identity and is not a role grant.
4. A role grant must be independently revocable and scope-aware; it does not create a tenant membership.
5. A student is tenant-owned through mandatory tenant_id; person_id is nullable and, when present, references people.id. A student need not have a tenant membership.
6. Every tenant-owned academic record must have an enforceable tenant-safe relationship to its parent entities. Prefer composite foreign keys over relying only on application filters.
7. enrollments reference same-tenant students and batches; academic_context_epochs reference a same-tenant enrollment.
8. Effective date intervals must satisfy valid_to IS NULL OR valid_to > valid_from.
9. Do not assume a single active enrollment; overlap/current-row rules remain blocked by OPEN-010/D-001 pending Academic Owner approval.
10. Historical enrollment and context rows must not be silently overwritten or deleted when academic placement changes.
11. System A actor foreign keys reference people.id, not auth.users.id; student references use tenant-qualified student keys.
12. System A has no authority to create, merge or delete shared identities through ordinary academic workflow commands.

## 5. Existing shared-core SQL assessment

Source inspected: feat/pulse-domain-core/supabase/migrations/0001_identity_and_academic_context.sql.

It currently creates five tables:

- public.tenants
- public.people
- public.tenant_memberships
- public.students
- public.academic_context_epochs

It does not yet provide the complete contract above:

| Gap | Required M0001 treatment |
|---|---|
| No Auth UID-to-person mapping | Add a dedicated mapping entity with approved provider/subject uniqueness and lifecycle |
| No persisted role grant model | Keep tenant_memberships separate from tenant_role_grants; grants are deferred according to authorization decisions |
| No centres or batches tables | Add canonical tables |
| Legacy academic_context_epochs.batch_id has no FK | Replace direct batch pointer with tenant-safe enrollment FK |
| No tenant-safe composite FK strategy | Enforce tenant-qualified student, enrollment and context references |
| TypeScript academic context has teacherIds, SQL has no teacher relation | Normalize into teaching_assignments; do not add a denormalized UUID array |
| No teaching assignment table | Defer to M0003 unless separately approved |
| No effective-dated role lifecycle | Resolve role-grant validity, revocation and scope rules before authorization implementation |

The existing SQL must not be copied unchanged into the canonical migration stream.

## 6. Approved tenant-safe identity and enrollment model — DEC-012

The owner selected Option B: tenant memberships are independent from student identity; students are tenant-owned with an optional person link; explicit enrollments connect students to batches. This supersedes the earlier student-to-membership composite-FK proposal.

- `tenant_memberships` has tenant_id and person_id, with tenant-scoped uniqueness and tenant-qualified keys.
- `students` has mandatory tenant_id and nullable person_id referencing people.id. Do not reference tenant_memberships from students.
- `students` has a tenant-qualified unique key, such as UNIQUE(tenant_id,id), for child references.
- `enrollments` references (tenant_id,student_id) and (tenant_id,batch_id), with effective interval and lifecycle fields.
- `academic_context_epochs` references (tenant_id,enrollment_id); it does not independently establish a batch relationship.
- Application joins alone are not an acceptable substitute for referential integrity.
- No constraint may assume one active enrollment until OPEN-010/D-001 is approved.

## 7. Auth identity mapping contract — OPEN-014

The physical design must decide:

- Auth provider namespace and subject identifier representation.
- Whether Supabase auth.users.id is the only supported subject or one provider among multiple.
- Uniqueness of provider + subject.
- Whether one person may link multiple Auth identities.
- Verification/claim trust state and who may create or relink mappings.
- What happens on Auth deletion, account recovery, merge and unlink.
- Whether mapping rows are immutable/audited and how stale sessions are revoked.

Do not store email as the canonical Auth key. Email can change and is not a stable actor identifier. Do not use raw_user_meta_data for authorization.

## 8. Role grant contract — OPEN-015 and OPEN-019–021

- tenant_memberships is membership/association only.
- Role/capability grants are separate records.
- A grant must include a tenant, person, role/permission reference, effective interval, grantor/provenance and revocation semantics.
- Resource scope must be explicit: tenant, centre, batch, student or another approved resource.
- A NULL scope must not silently mean global access.
- Role bundles, scope inheritance and separation-of-duties remain owner decisions.
- If authorization is deferred to M0002, M0001 must not expose application access that assumes roles already exist.

## 9. Centre, batch, enrollment and academic context contract — OPEN-017 and DEC-012

Required decisions:

- Centre naming and uniqueness within tenant.
- Whether a batch must belong to a centre or may be tenant-wide.
- Batch lifecycle and archival behavior.
- Academic year representation and normalization.
- Stream/class-level vocabulary and whether it is extensible.
- Student's concurrent active context/batch policy.
- Effective interval overlap rules and transfer semantics.
- Whether a context epoch captures centre, programme, stream, class and batch directly or references normalized enrolment records.

A batch UUID without a canonical table and tenant-safe FK is not acceptable in the final schema.

## 11. RLS and grants boundary

M0001 must not create a false sense of production security.

Before any table in an exposed schema is reachable by application roles:

- RLS is enabled.
- Table grants are explicitly reviewed; grants and RLS are separate controls.
- Policies enforce tenant association and appropriate role/resource scope.
- SELECT policies are tested independently from UPDATE policies.
- UPDATE policies include both USING and WITH CHECK.
- Sensitive identity/Auth mapping and role grant writes are restricted to trusted server-side operations.
- Views use security_invoker = true where caller RLS must apply.
- Prefer SECURITY INVOKER functions. Any SECURITY DEFINER exception requires fixed search_path, strict trusted actor validation, non-exposed placement and narrow EXECUTE grants.
- No application permission is inferred from a user-editable JWT metadata field.

Owner decision OPEN-029 selects the internal-only foundation. M0001 must not grant access to anon/authenticated or expose these objects through the Data API. A later security migration must implement and test the complete authorization boundary before application access.

M0001 is ready for implementation only when:

- [x] Canonical source branch and migration ownership approved: main is eventual canonical integration branch; current docs branch remains proposal branch (OPEN-013).
- [x] Auth identity mapping approved: dedicated person_auth_identities, unique Supabase Auth UUID subject, canonical people.id actor, trusted audited account linking (OPEN-014).
- [x] tenant_memberships association separated from effective-dated scoped tenant_role_grants (DEC-012).
- [x] Tenant-owned students with mandatory tenant_id and optional person_id; no membership FK (DEC-012).
- [x] Shared tenant-owned centres and batches approved; batch centre relationship same-tenant and optional only for tenant-wide batches (OPEN-017).
- [ ] Concurrent active enrollment/overlap policy is approved (OPEN-010/D-001 remains blocked; do not add single-active-enrollment uniqueness assumptions).
- [x] Subject/chapter catalogue excluded from M0001; catalogue ownership remains deferred (OPEN-011).
- [x] Teaching assignments deferred to M0003; OPEN-018 remains open for that migration.
- [x] Internal-only M0001 approved: no anon/authenticated grants or Data API exposure; later security migration required (OPEN-029).
- [ ] Exact object inventory, PK/FK/check/unique/index definitions are reviewed.
- [ ] Empty database replay passes on PostgreSQL 17.
- [ ] Two-tenant fixtures prove cross-tenant references fail.
- [ ] Auth identity resolution is unique and cannot be spoofed by user metadata.
- [ ] Role revocation and effective-date behavior pass tests if grants are included.
- [ ] Migration diff and Supabase advisors are reviewed.
- [ ] Recovery strategy and deployment environment are approved.

## 13. Non-goals and prohibitions

- Do not write executable SQL from this specification while blocking decisions remain open.
- Do not apply the historical shared-core migration unchanged.
- Do not apply the earlier System A initial schema unchanged.
- Do not introduce duplicate System A-local tenant, person, Auth user, student, centre, batch or membership authorities.
- Do not make Auth UID the academic actor FK.
- Do not use arrays such as teacherIds as a substitute for normalized scoped relationships.
- Do not add permissive RLS policies to make the application appear functional.
- Do not apply any DDL to the connected Supabase project as part of this specification.

**Implementation status:** Six owner decisions approved. Executable M0001 preparation is authorized, with OPEN-010 handled by avoiding active-context uniqueness assumptions and OPEN-011 handled by excluding catalogue references. No remote SQL has been applied.


## 14. Approved implementation baseline — 2026-11-07

The six owner approvals have been recorded in the Database Decision Register. The following implementation choices now govern preparation of the M0001 SQL candidate.

### 14.1 Exact M0001 object boundary

**Create or retain in the unified migration stream:**

1. `public.tenants` — canonical tenant identity.
2. `public.people` — canonical person identity.
3. `public.tenant_memberships` — person-to-tenant association only; independent of student identity.
4. `public.person_auth_identities` — dedicated mapping from Supabase Auth UUID to `people.id`.
5. `public.students` — tenant-owned identity with mandatory tenant_id and nullable person_id; no membership FK.
6. `public.centres` — tenant-owned centre identity.
7. `public.batches` — tenant-owned batch identity with optional same-tenant centre.
8. `public.enrollments` — tenant-safe effective-dated student-to-batch relationship.
9. `public.academic_context_epochs` — references same-tenant enrollment.

**Do not create in M0001:**

- `tenant_role_grants`: create in M0002 after OPEN-019/020/021 decisions. M0001 must not imply a role or permission from membership.
- `teaching_assignments`: defer to M0003; OPEN-018 remains open.
- Parent/guardian relationships: defer until relationship verification and field-purpose decisions close.
- Subject/chapter catalogues and curriculum FKs: exclude under OPEN-011.
- System A workflow tables, QBMS content, DTE taxonomy or difficulty records.

### 14.2 Identity and tenant-key contract

- Supabase Auth is the only authentication provider in the initial release scope.
- `person_auth_identities.auth_user_id` is unique and references the Auth subject UUID by value; do not add an FK to managed `auth.users` unless platform ownership and deletion lifecycle are explicitly reviewed.
- `person_auth_identities.person_id` references `public.people(id)` with RESTRICT semantics.
- A person may have more than one Auth identity only through a trusted, audited server-side linking workflow. A single Auth subject maps to at most one person.
- Email, display name and `raw_user_meta_data` are not identity or authorization keys.
- Add tenant-qualified keys to tenant_memberships; do not reference memberships from students.
- Add mandatory students.tenant_id and nullable students.person_id REFERENCES people(id); enforce UNIQUE(tenant_id,id).
- Add enrollments with tenant-qualified FKs to students and batches and effective interval fields.
- Add academic_context_epochs tenant-qualified FK to enrollments; remove direct batch linkage.

### 14.3 Centre, batch and context contract

- Centre codes are normalized for uniqueness within a tenant; names must be non-empty after trimming.
- Batch codes are normalized and unique within `(tenant_id, academic_year)`; names must be non-empty.
- A batch's optional `centre_id` must reference a centre in the same tenant.
- Centre and batch status use an explicit lifecycle; referenced records are archived/deactivated, not deleted.
- academic_context_epochs references enrollment; it does not independently establish a batch relationship.
- Preserve valid-time history. Do not add one-active-enrollment uniqueness or overlap constraints until OPEN-010/D-001 is approved.
- Keep existing `stream` and `class_level` domain checks only after comparing all current source values and product requirements; do not silently narrow valid academic values.

### 14.4 Initial security boundary

- M0001 is internal-only. Explicitly revoke table privileges from `anon` and `authenticated`; do not grant either role access to the identity objects.
- Enable RLS on each created/retained application table in the exposed schema, but do not create permissive policies in M0001.
- Do not create SECURITY DEFINER functions, views, triggers or application RPCs in this migration.
- Verify Data API exposed-schema configuration during implementation preflight. No table is to be exposed for application use until the later reviewed security migration.
- Do not infer that service-role use is safe in a browser; it remains server-only.
- The remote project remains untouched. Local replay and tests are the only permitted execution target for this phase.

### 14.5 Extension and schema drift handling

- Do not add `CREATE EXTENSION pgcrypto` solely to obtain `gen_random_uuid()`; PostgreSQL 17 provides the UUID generator. Include an extension only if a concrete object in this migration requires it and local preflight proves it is needed.
- The migration must fail clearly if it encounters incompatible pre-existing application objects. Do not use broad `IF NOT EXISTS` clauses to hide drift.
- Reconcile the historical five-table source migration into a new canonical migration; do not copy its old filename or apply it unchanged.

### 14.6 Remaining pre-SQL review gates

Before the timestamped migration is created, review:
- exact existing column types, names, defaults, ownership and constraints from the shared-core source;
- whether `public` remains the intended schema for internal-only objects or a non-exposed schema is preferred;
- exact normalized-code expression/index implementation and collation behavior;
- whether a unique one-student-per-tenant-association constraint matches all onboarding/transfer cases;
- Auth mapping lifecycle when an Auth account is deleted, disabled, recovered or linked/unlinked;
- current permitted stream/class values and whether they should remain extensible text codes.

These are implementation verification gates, not permission to broaden M0001 scope. Any change that alters an approved owner decision must return to the owner.

- OPEN-010: remains open; no one-active-context constraint.
- OPEN-011: remains open; catalogue excluded.
- OPEN-018: remains open; teaching assignments deferred to M0003.
- OPEN-019/020/021: remain open; role grants deferred to M0002.

## 15. Reconciliation hold — 2026-11-07

A later audit of `feat/system-a-abhyas-foundation` identified unresolved physical-contract differences. The current M0001 object contract is therefore a controlled proposal, not yet the final SQL-authoring baseline.

The owner has closed RECON-001/002/003 through DEC-012. Only RECON-004 (concurrent enrollment policy) remains blocked; M0001 must follow the approved Option B model.

- DEC-012 now selects tenant_memberships as the canonical association table.
- DEC-012 makes students tenant-owned with optional person_id and no membership FK.
- DEC-012 requires explicit enrollments and context epochs reference enrollment.
- D-001 concurrent-enrollment policy remains blocked pending Academic Owner approval.

DEC-012 supersedes only the earlier physical student/membership relationship. All other approved decisions remain in force. No SQL or remote DDL was created/applied as part of this reconciliation.
